name: Pale Ecru-Drab
lede: Pale Ecru-Drab is a pinkish grey from Ridgway's 1912 plates, among the most common colors in our painting archive, where Shen Zhou returns to it in more than half his works.

sections.title: A grey, close to Silver
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate XLVI, hue 13′′′′, tone f, scanned from an aged plate and so approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it in its own block [1]. Our library notes it sits close to the Crayola color Silver, within 6.5 units, and to [[warm-silver]], another separately sourced name, within 3.3 units [2].

Its nearest relatives in the graph are [[warm-silver]] and [[warm-silver]], almost the same, and [[oatmeal]] and [[dark-silver-pink]], close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Pale Ecru-Drab covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 1,100 works, more common than 87 per cent of our named colors [4]. The painter most devoted to it is Shen Zhou, in 7 of his 12 works here, about 5.2 times his museums' baseline [4]. It most often shares a canvas with [[warm-grey]] and [[linen]], at 10.0 and 5.2 times the expected rate [4]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is the year 1000, nine centuries before the name's own 1912 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].
